9397afbbdf14d1f13fe38facb428e18adabd7a60.summary: This page is an event listing for a BrightTalk webcast, 'The Sample: Beating the Malware Pinata', presented by Christopher Gardner of the Mandiant FLARE reverse engineering team and published 2022-05-05. It outlines talk topics such as analysing droppers, extracting payloads from process injection, and open-source intelligence. It is an event and marketing page, not a threat report, so no facts are recorded.

930cc42115fcbd879cf67403b12c3a3e4e347abe.summary: Researcher's archived 2022 analysis of a Korean-language HWP document lure, attributed by the author to North Korea-linked APT37 and to its ROKRAT operations. A malicious HWP OLE object runs a BAT script that launches PowerShell to load shellcode into memory through reflective DLL injection. The shellcode stager was offline, so the in-memory payload was not analysed. The attribution is the author's own judgement.

These are the speakers' opinions and predictions, not confirmed findings.

93b3d9455997fb6f28801426c0bcf0432eb87860.summary: Group-IB report on the Cobalt criminal group and its suspected joint operations with Anunak/Carbanak. It describes thefts from banks and financial services, including SWIFT, card processing, ATMs and payment gateways. Europol links the group to about one billion euros in thefts from 100 banks in 40 countries. It covers the March 2018 arrest of the group leader in Spain, May 2018 phishing campaigns impersonating security and bank brands, the CobInt backdoor and a PetrWrap ransomware variant. The report presents the joint-operation link as likely rather than proven.

939b3f78473a8b4c171ef36ae3e74817db77a8e3.summary: Anomali Threat Research reports that China-based cryptomining actor Rocke moved its command and control for the LSD malware from Pastebin to self-hosted subdomains in summer 2019, then to DNS TXT records with a DNS-over-HTTPS fallback in September 2019. The malware also gained exploitation of ActiveMQ (CVE-2016-3088) and Confluence (CVE-2019-3396), brute-forces SSH and Redis credentials, and installs a Monero miner. The report expects further exploitation and warns the payload could change to ransomware or a RAT.
